# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can touch the plate and wires but cannot see the display, light, colours, or printed markings. The plate is engraved with a distinctive eight-petalled floral symbol, and no wire properties are revealed by touch. I am telling Mute about the engraving so the manual can identify the required action; Deaf should inspect and report the visual information through the available channels.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a plate engraved with a distinctive eight-petalled floral symbol, like a small rosette or star-flower. The display, light, and wire contents reveal nothing to touch. Please consult the manual for this plate marking and obtain the visual bomb information from Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved question mark. Wires from left to right are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The previous message failed only because it attempted to pronounce an unnamed engraved mark. I will describe that mark in ordinary words instead, while relaying the display, light, wire colours, and Deaf’s description of the plate to Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light off, and wires left-to-right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Deaf sees the plate marking as a question mark; I feel the plate engraved with a distinctive eight-petalled floral rosette. Please use the manual to determine the required cut position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have not received the manual’s instruction yet, so cutting a wire would be unsafe. I am asking Mute to provide the required wire position explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual result. Given display 0, light off, plate marking question mark, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which exact wire position must I cut? I will wait for your instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has again signalled three upward gestures followed by right. I cannot determine the intended operation; do not act yet.

The gesture sequence is not available to me, and Deaf cannot determine its intended operation. Since no explicit wire position has reached me, I will not cut anything. I am asking Mute to state the instruction in words and numbers.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please state plainly in words: cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. Do not use gestures for this instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signals: three, then right. I see wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No explicit cut or connect instruction.

Mute’s gestures still do not provide an unambiguous spoken wire position or an operation. Deaf’s report confirms only “three, then right,” which is insufficient to safely act; I will not cut a wire based on that.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your signal is ambiguous. State the complete instruction in words, including the operation and exact wire position: for example, cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals three. This likely identifies wire 3, the blue wire, but no action has been specified. Do not cut or alter it yet.

The only usable new information is that Mute signals “three,” which may identify wire position 3, but no operation has been stated. I will not cut a wire without the manual’s explicit instruction. I am requesting a plain spoken instruction from Mute and warning Deaf that no action is authorized yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand your signal may identify wire position 3, but I still need the operation. Speak plainly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3, only if that is the manual instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals three, then a downward open hand. You signalled no. I do not have a confirmed action.

Mute’s latest sequence identifies wire position 3, followed by the operation signal. Since Mute cannot speak, the operation must be conveyed through the gesture code; the downward open-hand signal is the first clear operation indication received. With no other confirmed position, I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
